verdict.reasoning: Patient reports onset 'about fifteen minutes ago, I was gardening and ... was stung by wasp' and then 'I'm having quite shallow breath' plus 'I can definitely feel something in the lips, yeah' described as tingling by doctor.
Patient states 'I'm having quite shallow breath' and later confirms 'a bit of tightness, yeah' when asked about chest tightness.
When asked about rash, patient says 'Yes there's a bit of blotching,' which is consistent with a blotchy rash.
Doctor asks 'is there any swelling of your lips, you feel your throat is closing up?' and clarifies 'OK, but no swelling, yeah?'—indicating no throat/lip swelling noted.
Doctor asks 'Have you had anything like this before?' and patient answers 'Uh, no,' indicating this is the first episode.
Doctor asks 'have you taken anything at all for the blotching?' and patient replies 'I wouldn't even know what to take then,' indicating no medications taken yet.
In past history, patient says 'a bit of eczema.'
Patient states 'I have aerosinusitis, so yes, I do' when discussing antihistamine use, indicating a history of aerosinusitis.
When asked about antihistamines at home, patient answers 'Um, yes, I've used them for flying... so yes, I do,' indicating over-the-counter antihistamine at home.

Doctor asks 'Is there someone else at home with you?' and patient replies 'Yes, my wife can take me to the emergency room,' and later 'She's listening... she's on the phone,' showing he lives with his wife and she is present.

Doctor states 'what we are worried about is, you know, in case you develop an anaphylactic reaction' in the setting of wasp sting and 'breathing difficulties,' indicating suspected anaphylaxis with respiratory involvement.
Doctor advises 'I would like her to call the ambulance' and reiterates 'I'd like you to call the ambulance.'
Doctor says 'I'll ask her to give you the, um, antihistamine, in the meantime while the ambulance is coming.'
Transcript states only 'take yourself to hospital' and 'go to hospital straight away' with concern for anaphylaxis; it does not mention airway monitoring, IM adrenaline, or detailed ED management.
